question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{2}-1.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{2}-1,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}+1} & = \\ \frac{7-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}+1}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}-1} & = \\ \frac{(7-\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{2}-1)}{(\sqrt{2}+1)(\sqrt{2}-1)} & = \\ \frac{7\sqrt{2}-7-(\sqrt{2})^{2}+\sqrt{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}-(1)^{2}} & = \\ \frac{7\sqrt{2}-7-2+\sqrt{2}}{2-1} & = \\ \frac{8\sqrt{2}-9}{1} & = \\ 8\sqrt{2}-9\end{aligned}
$$
